newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds edge down, market nervously eyes punt.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds edge down, market nervously eyes punt.

text.p: Irish government bonds slipped back in thin afternoon trade on Friday as the uncertainty surrounding the Irish pound weighed on the market, dealers said.
"The main focus in the market is on the currency. There is a lot of chat about what the Central Bank might have to do," one trader said,
The Irish pound dipped briefly below 90 pence sterling, a key psychological level, this afternoon, before recovering to trade at 0.9010 by 1430 GMT as talk of a revaluation ran out of steam.
Dealers said they were now watching the central bank to see would it intervene to support the punt or raise interest rates to underpin it.
"The short end is nervous and we have underperformed the rest of Europe," one trader said.
By 1430 GMT, the six percent bond due 2001 was at 102.60 to yield 5.80 percent, down 17 pence from Thursday's close, while 10-year paper slipped 25 pence to 110.65 to yield 6.43 percent.
Dealers said the yield spread over bunds in the 10-year area had widened out to 90 basis points from 88 this morning.
But they noted that with the U.S. market closed for Independence Day and little economic data of note being released, volume was light.
